quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection. Oncoming traffic is blocking your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane of traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Do not start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on a bridge over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs warn drivers that the road curves sharply in the direction shown by the arrow. You may see several chevron signs throughout the curve.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Does smoking while driving distract you?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving abilities.
No, it helps you stay alert.
No, it is not a distraction.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you by taking your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Turn on your flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes. Grip the steering wheel tightly and stay in your lane. Slow down by releasing the gas pedal. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines are doubled in work zones.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert drivers to upcoming conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers to watch for bicycles crossing.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: At any intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Cars have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must get out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians should cross. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. It will hurt your driving skills. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Construction zones are dangerous. Orange signs warn you about construction ahead. This sign tells you a flagger is coming. Follow their directions.

questions.question: A speed restriction sign:

options.text: May be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.
Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Signs on curves and turns show a recommended speed for that area. Even if you feel safe going faster in good weather, slow down in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out as you are driving, you should:

options.text: Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.
Maintain your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the wheel tight and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the gas pedal slowly. Do not brake hard until you have control. Then brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means the action is not allowed. In this case, it means no right turn.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best thing to do is to:

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and go to sleep.
Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you remain in your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is unsafe.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the light like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the light like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Not turn on any vehicle lights.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of approaching vehicles or 500 feet behind another vehicle. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):
questions.explanation: Stop signs are octagonal (eight-sided). All eight-sided signs tell you to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol content depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Food in your stomach slows alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent intoxication or impairment from drinking too much.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn drivers about special situations or hazards ahead.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Watches what other drivers are doing
Travels at the same speed all the time

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers can get distracted. A defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train
Slow down and look for a train
Look for a train, then speed up
Do what the car ahead of you does

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing signal at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or oncoming trains.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, turning and curves are especially dangerous. Slow down before entering turns more than you normally would.

questions.question: You must pull over for an emergency vehicle:

options.text: No matter which direction it comes from
Only if it is behind you
Only if it is coming toward you

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it comes from
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it comes from behind or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and prepare drivers for road conditions and hazards. This sign tells drivers that traffic may come from the opposite direction.

questions.question: A bus is signaling to get back on the road after a stop. You must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there

questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus signaling to return to the road after stopping. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and prepare drivers for road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that a winding road is ahead and to adjust their speed.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. When you see a red, eight-sided sign, you must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn at this intersection.

questions.question: Pentagonal signs indicate:
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Be extra careful to watch for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without signals?

options.text: Always bring the car to a complete stop.
Slow down and be prepared to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.
Increase your speed to get across the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an unmarked railroad crossing. Look and listen for trains from both directions on any track. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait for it to pass before crossing.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you decrease your speed, the roadway becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: When you drive fast on wet roads, your tires lose their grip. Water builds up between your tires and the road. If you drive too fast, your tires will slide on the water instead of gripping the road. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Defending yourself against poor drivers by passing them.
Following the vehicle ahead of you closely.
Quickly changing lanes to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you notice dangerous situations before they become accidents. It helps you avoid aggressive, careless, or distracted drivers.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
Sound your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if you cannot drive all the way through it. Wait for traffic ahead to clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is an orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. It alerts you that the road shoulder ahead is lower than the paved road. Warning signs are yellow with black markings.

questions.question: The most common color of warning signs is:
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn you about unexpected road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction zones. This sign tells you that construction work is starting ahead. Be careful and watch for workers and equipment.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.
Drive faster than the traffic on the freeway.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match the freeway traffic. This helps you blend in smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: In cold weather, shaded areas freeze faster than sunny areas. Trees and buildings create shade that keeps roads colder. These shaded areas also dry last.

questions.question: Which idea does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Know that tinted windows make it harder to see at night.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking at oncoming headlights hurts your night vision. Your eyes contract when hit by bright light. When the car passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to darkness. During this time, you cannot see the road well.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous AND speeding can kill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous AND speeding can kill.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 mph, survival is very unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make unsafe moves to pass you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are near.
Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
Go carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only for traffic on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must make a full stop. Let pedestrians and vehicles pass safely. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means something is prohibited. This sign means you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows rules you must follow. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before braking.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops are dangerous. Check mirrors before stopping so cars behind you have time to react. Release the gas pedal first to slow down, then brake gently. This activates your brake lights and gives other drivers warning.
